relations.rationale: The workshop setting has no clear bearing on whether Uma brought a first-aid kit; the two claims describe unrelated matters.

The robotics workshop setup described in A has no connection to Ben and Quinn's shift schedules mentioned in B; they involve different subjects and contexts.

B describes an organizational detail (numbered worktables) that fits naturally within the setting established by A, where multiple tables of components could easily get mixed up. A makes B plausible and coherent but doesn't strictly require it.
Being the lead volunteer makes it plausible and expected that Gus would arrive early to help set up, since lead volunteers typically take initiative in preparation tasks.
Being the lead volunteer is a role/status claim unrelated to physical height comparison with Quinn; neither implies anything about the other.
Being the lead volunteer says nothing about physical height, so claim A has no bearing on the height comparison in claim B.
Claim A describes Gus's early arrival and helping with setup, which has no logical bearing on what Ben was wearing when he came in. These involve different people and unrelated details.

Claim A concerns Gus arriving early to help with registration, while claim B describes robots with obstacle-avoiding sensors, likely at some event Gus helped set up for. There is no logical or causal connection between these two statements as given.
Wearing a green jacket has no bearing on where Ben chose to sit; the two facts are independent details about Ben.
Claim A describes Ben's appearance upon arrival, while claim B describes the timing of Rosa's arrival relative to Ben's. These concern different subjects and facts with no logical connection.
A describes Ben's clothing when he arrived, which has no bearing on whether Ben and Rosa worked different shifts. The two claims concern unrelated topics.
